label: MEV protection
summary: Define a specific adversary, protected flow and failure policy for hook-enforced ordering or execution controls.
requiredFacts: Exact MEV adversary and protected user harm: sandwich, backrun, frontrun, censorship, last look or another named threat
Protection mechanism, trust assumptions, ordering source, expiry and behavior when protection is unavailable
Which traders, routers, order sources and swap paths receive or bypass protection
Price, slippage, fee, refund and revert policy for protected and unprotected execution
Operator, signer, sequencer, relayer or service authority and compromise recovery
requiredTests: Named attacker simulations with measurable protected-user outcomes
Protection unavailable, stale, censored, reordered, duplicated and bypassed behavior
Router, direct PoolManager and unsupported order-source paths
Price, slippage, fee, refund and revert conservation
Operator or signer compromise, rotation and permissionless exit
risks: A vague MEV claim can imply protection that the mechanism does not provide
Trusted ordering or private flow can introduce censorship, leakage or operator extraction
Protection rules can block compatible routers or create denial of service
